## Worksheet 1.7 — Introduction to Limits and Continuity

::: {.callout-note title="Problem 1"}
Consider the function $f(w) = \dfrac{\sqrt{w}-1}{w-1}$.

a. What is the domain of $f$?
b. Fill out the data table below:

| $w$    | 0.9 | 0.99 | 0.999 | 1.001 | 1.01 | 1.1 |
|--------|-----|------|-------|-------|------|-----|
| $f(w)$ |     |      |       |       |      |     |

c. What value does $f(w)$ appear to be approaching as $w$ approaches 1?
d. Write your observation from part (c) using limit notation: $\lim_{w\to a} f(w) = L$
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Problem 2"}
The physics department drops a watermelon off the top of the DMTI building. Suppose this watermelon falls for 1.5 seconds before it hits the ground.

a. Let $s(t)$ be the watermelon's speed $t$ seconds after it was dropped. Sketch a graph of $s(t)$ on the interval $0 \le t \le 3$. Is $s(t)$ continuous on this interval?
b. Let $h(t)$ be the watermelon's height above the ground $t$ seconds after it was dropped. Sketch a graph of $h(t)$ on the interval $0 \le t \le 3$. Is $h(t)$ continuous on $0 \le t \le 3$?
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Problem 3"}
Let

$$
h(x) = \begin{cases} ax^2+2 & \text{if } x<1 \\ 4 & \text{if } x=1 \\ -3x+b & \text{if } x>1 \end{cases}
$$

a. [Here is a link to a graph of $h(x)$ in Desmos.](https://www.desmos.com/calculator/k9s00vtasu) Use the sliders to help you guess the values of $a$ and $b$ that make $h(x)$ continuous at $x=1$.
b. Verify your answer to part (a) algebraically.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Problem 4"}
A 0.6 mL dose of a drug is administered to a patient steadily for half a second. At the end of this time, the quantity $Q$ of the drug in the body starts to decay exponentially. The continuous decay rate of the drug is 0.2% per second.

a. Let $Q(t)$ be the amount of drug in the body $t$ seconds after the drug began to be administered. Do you expect $Q(t)$ to be continuous for $t>0$?
b. Find a formula for $Q(t)$.
:::

## Worksheet 1.8 — Concept of a Limit

::: {.callout-note title="Problem 1 — Baked Potato"}
A baked potato is placed in an oven. Let $P(x)$ be a function modeling the temperature of the potato $x$ minutes after it has been placed in the oven.

a. Sketch what you think the graph of $P(x)$ should look like.
b. Do you expect $\lim_{x\to\infty} P(x)$ to exist? If so, what would this value represent in the context of the problem? If not, why?
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Problem 2 — Table of Values"}
Let $f(x) = \dfrac{x^2+2x-3}{x+1}$ and $g(x) = \dfrac{x^2-2x-3}{x+1}$.

a. Fill out the following table of values:

| $x$    | -1.1 | -1.01 | -1.001 | -0.999 | -0.99 | -0.9 |
|--------|------|-------|--------|--------|-------|------|
| $f(x)$ |      |       |        |        |       |      |
| $g(x)$ |      |       |        |        |       |      |

b. Use the table to guess the value of the following limits. If the limit does not exist, write DNE, $\infty$, or $-\infty$ as appropriate.

   i. $\lim_{x\to -1^-} f(x)$
   ii. $\lim_{x\to -1^+} f(x)$
   iii. $\lim_{x\to -1^-} g(x)$
   iv. $\lim_{x\to -1^+} g(x)$
:::
